maria: Quick summary of the eviction-sim runs I kicked off overnight. Wanted eyes before we push to canary.
kevin: Dropped the raw sim logs into the s3 link in the ticket. TL;DR: granular-evict (age+freq buckets) cuts steady-state KV residency ~18% for 24h streaming sessions.
ashok: Nice. Any regressions on latency?
julia: Yes — p95 token latency for short-turn generation increased ~12% on the sim because we saw more KV misses and synchronous page loads during tool loops.
maria: Here's the important bit from the profiler: page-loads are more frequent but smaller; net async io ops up 30%, but blocking tail hops up.
kevin: Paste from the sim summary:```
policy: granular-evict-v3
24h-session: residency_drop=18%
avg_tokens_per_sec=48 -> unchanged
p50_token_latency=14ms -> +1ms
p95_token_latency=62ms -> +7ms
cache_hit_rate=0.86 -> down from 0.91
background_compact_rate=+10%
```
julia: That hit_rate drop explains the tail. We evict more aggressively on older spans but we also fragmented some pages which forced more small-copy kernel work.
ashok: Did kernel selection change at all during these runs? Could a different GEMM/attention kernel handle the smaller KV page sizes better? e.g., a kernel with lower startup cost might help p95.
kevin: I instrumented kernel binder traces — we see ~22% increase in binder churn when page sizes shrink (more frequent kernel rebinds for small batches). Not huge but noticeable in p99 CPU cycles.
maria: Options: 1) tweak eviction thresholds to keep high-frequency prefixes pinned, 2) coalesce small page loads into batched I/O, or 3) change kernel selection heuristic to prefer low-latency kernels for batches flagged with many small KV fetches.
julia: I prototyped a cheap heuristic: when kv_page_fetch_count_per_request > 4, prefer kernel-low-startup. In microbenchit, that recover ~5ms of p95 but adds +3% avg cycles.
kevin: There's also a batching angle: current dynamic batching groups by arrival window only. If we add a micro-grouping by KV-affinity (requests that likely have overlapping keys), we can increase local cache hits inside a batch and reduce IO. Simulation shows that micro-grouping recovers ~6% hit-rate for tool-loop patterns.
maria: Sample config snippet for granular-evict-v3 (from experiments):```json
{
  "evict_buckets": ["hot","warm","cold"],
  "hot_ttl_s": 28800,
  "warm_ttl_s": 3600,
  "cold_ttl_s": 300,
  "min_pin_score": 0.75,
  "coalesce_small_fetches": true
}
```
julia: coalesce_small_fetches toggled to true in sim; that's the change that reduced many of the small kernel churns.
ashok: Any stability regressions noted? OOMs or GC spikes?
kevin: No OOMs. We did see higher IO queue depth sometimes which bumped host-side wall-clock when many sessions streamed concurrently. perf-bot: CI perf check -> build 4332/gcj: p95 increase flagged (investigate) :warning:
maria: My recommendation: enable coalesce_small_fetches + pin threshold increase (min_pin_score 0.8) behind a runtime flag for canary. Also enable kernel-low-startup for micro-batches with kv_fetch_count > 4.
julia: Agreed. Run a 48h canary on a subset of dedicated pools with heavy tool-loop traffic (beta customers). Collect: kv_hit_rate, p50/p95 token latency, kernel-bind events per minute, io_queue_depth.
kevin: I'll add the telemetry slices and a dashboard. Will also add a small smoke test that exercises long-tool loops to catch regressions early.
maria: Action items: @kevin add dashboard & sim artifacts to the ticket; @julia add kernel heuristic toggle; @ashok coordinate canary pools and rollout flag.
ashok: On it. Can we schedule the canary for tomorrow morning UTC?
maria: Yes. If we see p95 regressions >10% vs baseline, we auto-roll back.
kevin: One more note — the sim used 4KB page granularity. If we increase page coalescing at the runtime level to 8KB for streaming chat, eviction behavior improves but memory fragmentation goes up for short sessions. Need to weigh tradeoffs.
julia: We'll capture fragmentation metrics too: average free-run-length, page-slab-util.
maria: Thanks everyone — let's convene a short sync after 24h canary to decide final policy. :thumbsup:
